title: How big a keyword-spotting model fits a real Tiny Tapeout tile once the hidden layer goes past 64 units?
lede: Synthesising the streaming keyword-spotting engine at 96, 128, 192 and 256 hidden units (SKY130 HD, Yosys): area grows about 250 µm² per unit, so H = 128 (0.752 accuracy, 4-bit) needs a 2x2 tile (75,603 µm²) against a 1x2 (36,347 µm²) for H = 64 (0.737): +0.015 accuracy for twice the tile; H = 256 needs 4x2 at 50% utilisation, and its 8-bit layer-2 accumulator overflows 20 bits on a random model.
summary: accel-ttsizes stopped its sweep at H = 64 so larger tiles had nothing to hold. This project synthesises the same streaming engine at H = 96, 128, 192 and 256 (weights of 2, 3, 4 and 8 bits, 70 and 120 inputs, 64 synthesis runs with the RTL checked against the integer reference in Icarus Verilog) and finds the smallest of Tiny Tapeout's 12 real tile sizes that holds each at 100, 70 and 50% utilisation. Area is roughly linear at about 250 µm² per hidden unit (H = 128: 36,411–40,747 µm²; H = 256: 68,606–72,897). The most accurate model, H = 128 with 4-bit weights (0.752, from accel-kws, which had trained it), needs a 2x2 tile; the best 1x2 model (H = 64, 0.737) is 0.015 less accurate, and a 2x2 is 2.08× the area of a 1x2. A 24-bit accumulator adds 0.1–2.1% area. At H = 256 with 8-bit weights, a random model overflows the 20-bit accumulator, so larger models need a wider one or a trained-model check. Utilisation is assumed, area is synthesis-only, and accuracy above H = 64 was not retrained here (the dataset host was unreachable) and has not been checked against the tile's bias and accumulator limits.
